findings.location: §8B 'What is being independently rediscovered' — 'The isotonic cone is **convex** and takes the ordering as an input; the GARP-consistent set is a **non-convex union over orderings** ... The order-conditional half is solved; the combinatorial half is not'
findings.issue: The single sentence carrying the report's most load-bearing technical distinction asserts that the ordering search is the unsolved half, which the project's own method note flatly contradicts: with the data fixed the Afriat inequalities are already an LP requiring no ordering search, and Demuynck & Rehbeck's multiplier-free ordinal characterisation (Theorem 2, IP-1..IP-4) absorbs the ordering into T(T-1) binaries inside ONE MILP whose constraints are linear jointly in utilities, prices and quantities — so there is no outer search over orderings to solve.
findings.evidence: docs/METHOD_NOTE_Q3.md, §'The question, precisely stated' ('With the data fixed, the Afriat inequalities are already a linear program — no ordering search is required') and §'RECOMMENDED FORMULATION' ('A single MILP built on the multiplier-free ordinal characterisation ... no outer search over orderings'); research/comparisons.md Tension 3.
findings.recommendation: Split the one sentence into the three claims that actually survive, and drop the claim that the combinatorial half is unsolved. Keep: (a) what fails to transfer from the convex case is the GUARANTEE — isotonic projection onto a convex cone containing the truth is non-expansive in L2, and that property does not survive a union of polyhedra, so [3]'s 'weakly closer to ground truth' theorem has no analogue; (b) what is genuinely missing is the worked OBJECTIVE (Demuynck & Rehbeck's Average Quantity Error, sketched in two sentences); (c) the real construction difficulty is that promoting the bundles to decision variables makes the revealed-preference relation itself endogenous, so there is no outer scalar to bisect as there is for CCEI. State explicitly that the ordering search per se is a solved encoding, not an open problem, so the distinction rests on the guarantee and the objective rather than on tractability.

findings.location: §2B 'The severity layer and its complexity stratification' — 'the severity layer is computationally stratified in a way that maps onto repair difficulty ... they solve all three hard indices in under two seconds ... Hardness is asymptotic; tractability is a statement about the operating point'
findings.issue: The report borrows tractability from the MEASUREMENT problems (Houtman–Maks, average Varian, minimum cost — deletion/deflation objectives over fixed data) and lets it stand as a statement about REPAIR difficulty, which is exactly the objective-swap the method note warns against; it also states NP-hardness without carrying the number of goods, when the deletion problem is polynomial at K=2 and NP-complete only from K=3.
findings.evidence: docs/METHOD_NOTE_Q3.md, §'Why measurement is easy and construction is not' ('the measurement timings in docs/COMPUTE_NOTE.md do not transfer'), §'Boodaghians & Vetta' ('two-commodity markets ... polynomial time solvable ... three-commodity ... NP-complete'; 'Any complexity claim the paper makes must carry its K'), and §'RECOMMENDED FORMULATION' (the weighted-L2 least-squares version is a convex MIQP needing a commercial solver, not the MILP that solves in <2s).
findings.recommendation: Insert a qualifying clause after the two-second timing that (i) those timings are for indices computed over FIXED data with a combinatorial or scalar-bisection oracle, and do not transfer to a program in which the bundles are decision variables and the revealed-preference relation is therefore endogenous; (ii) the L2 version of the perturbation objective is a MIQP rather than a MILP; and (iii) attach the K-dependence to the NP-hardness sentence (polynomial at two goods, NP-complete from three), which §9C already knows but §2B does not say.

findings.location: §2C 'The repair layer, and its one missing cell' — 'Imposing a fixed strict-preference margin does the same job operationally, converting an unattained infimum into an attained minimum and a silent failure into a reported parameter.'
findings.issue: The margin is presented as an operational technicality with no citation, and the two consequences that matter are suppressed: what 'continuous but inaccurate' MEANS operationally is that the least-squares distance can read exactly 0 on data that violate GARP, and a fixed margin does not compute the projection — it computes a γ-margin projection onto a strictly smaller CLOSED SUBSET of the GARP-consistent set, so the reported distance is a γ-indexed upper bound on the object the report names.
findings.evidence: docs/METHOD_NOTE_Q3.md, §'Chen, Lanier & Quah' ('the LS index can report a distance of exactly 0 for a dataset that violates GARP'; 'argmin is empty') and §'RECOMMENDED FORMULATION' ('be explicit in the paper that the program computes the γ-margin projection, which is a projection onto a closed subset of the GARP-consistent set. Report γ and show the distance is insensitive to it across two or three decades'); vault note goodness-of-fit-and-utility-estimation-whats-possible-and-whats-not.
findings.recommendation: Expand the closedness passage by two sentences. First, spell out the operational content of 'inaccurate': an index can report zero distance on a GARP-violating dataset, which is a silent failure mode for any operator that minimises it. Second, state plainly that a fixed strict-preference margin γ buys attainment by shrinking the target to a closed subset, so what is computed is THE γ-margin projection and not THE minimal repair, that γ must be reported and swept, and that the resulting distance is an upper bound on the least-squares index. Do not let the margin pass as an implementation detail.

findings.location: Lede paragraph 2 ('Where an operator projects onto the same set its outcome metric grades, gains are near-automatic and near-tautological') and §7C 'The rule: target alignment between operator and metric'
findings.issue: The report's own strongest original claim has a counter-case sitting in its own census table: row 12, the axiom-term fine-tune [6], has maximal operator/metric alignment — the operator is a sum of axiom penalties and the metric IS axiom compliance — and the reported sign is negative (independence 0.8000 and transitivity 0.9583, both below baseline, on the risk-averse target; independence falling 0.948 → 0.857 → 0.496 across the logit-scale sweep). Perfect target alignment therefore does not make gains near-automatic, and the report never confronts this against its own rule.
findings.evidence: The draft's own §3B and §6A table row 12, sourced to vault note 260726288-the-innate-economic-preferences-of-language-models [6]; the draft's §7D already records the mechanism ('enforcing one axiom can consume another') but never connects it to §7C.
findings.recommendation: Qualify the 'near-automatic and near-tautological' claim in the lede and add a sentence to §7C conceding row 12 as a counter-case: when the metric is a VECTOR of axioms rather than a single set, target alignment on one component does not protect the others, so the rule holds for a scalar metric defined by the projection target and fails when the graded object is multi-axiom. This is a concession the rule can absorb; leaving it unstated is what makes the rule look post-hoc.

findings.location: §6A 'Census of Interventions Found' — 'Twelve entries clear all three tests, covering eleven distinct systems' and the '**Excluded, and why**' paragraph
findings.issue: At least two qualifying systems in the vault are absent from both the table and the excluded list, so the count that the report calls 'auditable' is wrong rather than merely conservative. ELSPR (AAAI 2026) filters an evaluator LLM's preference training data by strongly-connected-component analysis of a tournament graph, removing exactly the pairs that induce non-transitivity, and reports a 13.8% reduction in the fine-tuned evaluator's non-transitivity with human validation of the discarded data (34.4% vs 52.6% inter-annotator agreement). It clears (i), (ii) and (iii) under the report's own rule, and it is the ML front's Houtman–Maks — maximal consistent subset by deletion — which §8B's 'cycle deletion' rediscovery paragraph misses entirely. Separately, 'From Drift to Coherence' ships both an inference-time and a training-time martingale-coherence intervention and is currently represented only second-hand through [7] in table row 10.
findings.evidence: Vault notes 250517691-elspr-evaluator-llm-training-data-self-purification-on-non-transitive (arXiv:2505.17691, AAAI 2026) and 260617832-from-drift-to-coherence-stabilizing-beliefs-in-llms (arXiv:2606.17832); also 240514758-axioms-for-ai-alignment-from-human-feedback (NeurIPS 2024), a peer-reviewed predecessor to [8] that proves BTL and its generalizations fail social-choice axioms and constructs reward rules with axiomatic guarantees, missing from both the table and the excluded list.
findings.recommendation: Add ELSPR as a training-time transitivity-enforcement row (deletion operator, non-exogenous metric) and either promote 'From Drift to Coherence' to its own row or cite it as the primary behind row 10; add the NeurIPS 2024 axiomatic reward-learning paper to §5A and to the excluded/specified list so the claim that [8] is one of only two formal guarantees is not overstated. Update the '{twelve entries / eleven systems}' counts accordingly, and add ELSPR to §8B's cycle-deletion paragraph as the ML-side rediscovery of Houtman–Maks.

findings.location: §9B 'Half two: populated but unidentified' — 'or the treatment is binary rather than graded, so no dose–response curve exists to read' (and §5B, which discusses [13] only as 'the better-controlled replication ... nine wins to eight with one tie')
findings.issue: A nine-level dose–response curve on coherence weighting IS published, in the very paper the report treats as a replication: [13]'s Appendix C.4, Table 5 traces λ ∈ {−2, −1, −0.5, 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 2} against downstream length-controlled win rate, giving a clean inverted U with an interior optimum at λ = +1.0 (41.90), a monotone decline into the cyclic-first regime (40.21 → 38.66 → 37.27), a span of 4.63 LC.WR points, and flat response length across the sweep. The report's blanket 'the treatment is binary' clause is therefore false as stated, and it also silently drops the fact that this curve points PRO-transitivity — counter-evidence to the acceptance camp that the report would otherwise want.
findings.evidence: audit/ITEM2_occupants_C.md §B.6 ('Appendix C.4, Table 5 — nine λ levels traced against downstream generation quality'), vault note 260517342-transitivity-meets-cyclicity [13]; research/comparisons.md Tension 5 explicitly instructs that any priority claim be rewritten around object, dose metric and outcome exogeneity.
findings.recommendation: Add the curve to §5B or §7 and re-scope the §9B clause. Report the shape and the authors' own reading ('λ > 0 generally leads to better performance … λ < 0 consistently underperforms'), then distinguish it on the three grounds the reconciliation names: the dose is an early-training SCHEDULE TILT on a component of a learned third-party preference proxy rather than a quantity of incoherence removed, the endpoints (pure BT, pure cyclic) are not on the curve, and the outcome is an automated-judge win rate. Replace 'the treatment is binary rather than graded, so no dose–response curve exists' with a statement that the one published curve doses a model-internal mixing weight, not a coherence index, and is scored by a preference judgment.

findings.location: §3A 'CCEI averages above 0.997 ... a regime of limited test power', §7F 'flagship efficiency indices already sit at 0.994 to 1.000', §9C 'points to the regime where minimal repair is cheap'
findings.issue: Every near-ceiling CCEI in the report is read as a substantive fact about agents, with no power correction anywhere — no Bronars power, no Selten area, no predictive success — even though the project's own standing rule forbids reporting a CCEI without one, and even though the formal result that GARP's empirical content collapses exponentially in the number of goods is in the vault and uncited. A high CCEI under a low-power design means the test could not have failed, and a near-vacuous test makes the very projection operator the report proposes near-degenerate.
findings.evidence: audit/BRONARS_NOTE.md (Beatty & Crawford: pass rate 0.957 at area 0.912, i.e. 8.8% power, predictive success 0.045; the design behind [30] has 99.9% Bronars power but 7.9–26.3% bootstrap power on its own model observations; 'Bronars power is necessary, not sufficient'); vault note 260529361-the-empirical-content-of-revealed-preference-in-high-dimensions (Crawford & Tian 2026: for fixed T, Selten's Area → 1 exponentially in K; K=24, T=10 gives area 0.9996).
findings.recommendation: Insert a short passage — best placed in §3A with a back-reference from §7F — stating that unconditional test power and conditional (bootstrap/PURP) power are different questions, that published LLM CCEI ceilings come from two-good designs whose power must be reported alongside the index, and that GARP's empirical content falls exponentially in the number of goods, so any move to a richer commodity space trades power for realism. Then qualify the §7F 'the lever may not exist' inference: a ceiling index is consistent with either a coherent agent or an unfailable test, and the two have not been separated. Correct the loose '[30] is a regime of limited test power' phrase, which is wrong unconditionally (99.9% Bronars) and right only conditionally.

findings.location: §7F 'Can the instrument bear the inference? The answer is scale-dependent' — '**The reliability objection is therefore scale-dependent.** It is live for small models ... and largely inert for flagship systems, whose indices are format-stable.'
findings.issue: The report resolves rhetorically what the pipeline's own cross-locus reconciliation flags as the single most dangerous UNRESOLVED tension, and it does so by treating format-insensitivity as reliability. They are different constructs: the PNAS finding is an intraclass-correlation failure driven by low BETWEEN-subject variance, and a flagship pool whose indices all sit between 0.994 and 1.000 has almost no between-model variance — that is the PNAS failure mode instantiated, not refuted. No per-model test–retest ICC on fixed budget sets with fresh contexts has ever been measured.
findings.evidence: research/comparisons.md Tension 1 ('There is no third reading available in which format sensitivity is large and the index is a stable trait ... Both loci name the same thing that would change their position: a measured per-model ICC. That makes it a genuine open question and it must be flagged as one') and the Step 8 update ('the draft must not cite this source as reassurance about reliability without also citing it as a threat to headroom').
findings.recommendation: Downgrade the bolded resolution to a conditional and add one sentence distinguishing format-invariance from test–retest reliability, noting that no per-model ICC exists and that near-zero between-model variance at the ceiling reproduces rather than answers the PNAS diagnosis. Keep the existing single-study caveat, and extend it to §9D, where the same unreplicated result is used to forecast that repair migrates to small models.

findings.location: §4D 'What the two poles actually disagree about' — 'The apparent enforce-versus-accept dispute concerns the object of the operator, not whether repair destroys information. ... It is not, and has never been, an argument that projecting a single agent's realised choice sequence onto a consistent set is harmful.'
findings.issue: This reconciliation is stated for the whole acceptance pole but is only true of the Nash family, and it contradicts two things the report itself asserts twelve and forty lines earlier: [37] argues that a bounded agent complying with the coherence axioms must give up approximate optimality with respect to its own objective — a harm claim about a single agent, not an existence claim — and [42]'s exact loss decomposition prices what enforcing scalar representability costs in representational fidelity, which is precisely 'repair destroys information'. §5C then makes a third harm argument in the report's own voice (projecting a scalarisation-manufactured cycle re-derives the losing baseline).
findings.evidence: The draft's own §4A ('coherent expected-utility maximization is generally intractable, so a bounded agent that insists on complying with the axioms must give up even approximate optimality'), §4B ([42]'s agreement term), and §5C; vault notes 260810327 / the Philosophical Studies entry [37] and 260600291-the-representation-rationalizability-tradeoff-in-reward-learning [42].
findings.recommendation: Narrow the claim to the Nash/maximal-lottery family by name, and add a sentence conceding that the acceptance pole DOES contain harm-grounds objections to single-agent repair — the bounded-rationality intractability argument and the representation–rationalizability trade-off — so that the report's later position rests on those objections being about learned preference MODELS and about optimality under compute limits, not on nobody having made them.

findings.location: §8C 'Each side holds the corrective the other needs' — 'What it lacks is a cardinal dose: it counts cycles and reports non-transitivity rates [2][53] where the economics side has five graded indices'
findings.issue: The claim that the ML front has no cardinal severity measure is contradicted by three items the report itself cites or holds in the vault: [55]'s cyclic energy (a continuous circulation magnitude tested against a parametric bootstrap null at p = 0.008), [49]'s Hodge curl-flow component (an orthogonal, continuous measure of the irreducibly cyclic part), and the MCHF seminorm ‖U‖_⊕, defined as the infimum distance from a pairwise utility to the additively separable (scalar-representable) set — which is literally a minimum-perturbation-to-rationalizability index, and which governs a convergence rate and a first-order agreement result between NLHF and RLHF.
findings.evidence: Vault notes 260704590-attention-limited-reward-learning [55], 260107158-the-covariate-assisted-bayesian-intransitive-bradley-terry-model-via-combinatorial-hodge-theory [49], and 260622652-a-markov-chain-approach-to-preference-alignment (‖U‖_⊕ = inf over g,f of ‖U − g ⊕ f‖_∞).
findings.recommendation: Qualify the sentence: the ML front's DEPLOYED operators and ablations report counts and rates, but the front does possess cardinal intransitivity magnitudes — cyclic energy, the Hodge curl norm, and the additive-separability seminorm — that nobody has used as a dose axis for an intervention. That is a sharper and more defensible gap than 'it lacks a cardinal dose', and it strengthens rather than weakens the report's §9C open cell.

findings.location: Lede paragraph 3 ('Every implemented operator acts on a preference proxy — a judging model's rankings ... Nothing in the corpus takes an agent's own realised choices over budget sets') and §6B 'The diagonal'
findings.issue: The distinction between repairing a judge's pairwise rankings and repairing an agent's own choice sequence is asserted rather than defended, and it is doing enormous load-bearing work. Under the standard abstract definition — rationalizability of a choice function over menus — an LLM judge choosing between two responses IS an agent choosing from a two-element menu, and repairing its cycles IS enforcing an acyclicity condition on its own choice function; [1]'s Kemeny repair acts on the model's own stated pairwise preferences, not on a third party's. Budget sets and prices are Afriat's particular instantiation, not the definition, and the vault contains a price-free revealed-preference application where rationalizability is exactly an acyclicity condition on a graph.
findings.evidence: Vault notes dutch-books-and-money-pumps-rectifying-vulnerabilities-in-llms-through-rationali [1] (Kemeny repair of the model's OWN intransitive pairwise preferences) and 251223352-revealed-preference-analysis-of-shapley-scarf-housing-markets (rationalizability tested as acyclicity of a directed graph with no prices and no budget sets).
findings.recommendation: Add one or two sentences making the distinction defensible on stated grounds rather than by assertion: what the budget-set instantiation buys is (a) a cardinal, money-metric dose (CCEI, money-pump ratio) that a tournament over responses does not define, (b) an outcome denominated in the same units as the perturbation, and (c) a menu structure the experimenter sets rather than one the judge is handed. Concede in the same breath that under the abstract choice-function definition, entries 1, 2, 3 and 12 do repair an agent's own choice function, so the unoccupied cell is narrower than 'nobody repairs an agent's own choices'.

findings.location: §7C 'The rule: target alignment between operator and metric' — 'The prediction is falsifiable: an information-adding coherence operator should improve coherence and accuracy together, an information-removing one should trade them off.'
findings.issue: The general form of the rule carries two clauses that are available disjunctively, so each of the eight outcome readings can be rescued by whichever clause fits, and the report does not say what JOINT pattern would falsify it. The information-sign clause already has a strain inside the report's own corpus: rejection sampling onto the GARP-consistent region [5] removes information by construction yet improves an exogenous metric, and is rescued only by clause one — which is the pattern of a rule fitted after the fact to eight cases with two free parameters.
findings.evidence: The draft's own §7A/§7C treatment of [5] and [2]; the number of outcome readings the rule is fitted to is eight, stated in §7G.
findings.recommendation: Add a sentence naming the falsifying observation for the conjunction, not for each clause separately — e.g. an information-removing operator enforcing an axiom that IS true of the outcome's generating process which nonetheless degrades an exogenous metric — and concede that with eight readings and two clauses the rule is a hypothesis generated from the census rather than one tested on it. This costs the report nothing and protects the claim it flags as its own.
